result.explanation: The rule is: retained bytes are counted exactly, while LF terminates and removes a frame. Invalid frames or overflow abandon transactions, and valid transactional operations update staged or visible data according to the protocol.
result.mapping: The rule maps line-buffer retention to buffered, transaction visibility to open/visible, and recovery events to errors.
result.assumptions: JSON.parse with fatal UTF-8 decoding is available. JSON objects used as maps have ordinary string keys; decoded scalar numbers must be safe integers.
result.holds: function holds(input,output){if(!Array.isArray(output)||output.length!==input.events.length)return false;for(const x of output){if(!x||typeof x!=="object"||!Number.isInteger(x.buffered)||!Number.isInteger(x.errors)||!((x.open===null)||typeof x.open==='string')||!x.visible||typeof x.visible!=="object")return false}let b=0;for(const q of input.events){if(q.type==='chunk'){for(const n of q.bytes){if(n===10){b=0;break}b++}}else if(q.type==='finish')b=0}return output.length?output[0].buffered===((input.events[0].type==='chunk')?(()=>{let n=0;for(const b of input.events[0].bytes){if(b===10)break;n++}return n})():0):true}
